text:
Ilya Mikheyev signed a four-year deal with Tampa Bay on July 1 after two seasons in Chicago, and so far he's given the Lightning what they paid for: 5 goals and 8 points in 22 games on 15:05 a night, all at even strength or shorthanded. His goal against Edmonton on Thursday, a rebound, was his first in seven games.

His finishing is a little warm. He's shooting 16.1%, at the top end of our range for him, on 3.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances). The more interesting number is relative: the Lightning's five-on-five share of expected goals is 7.0 points worse with him on than without. That fits what Evolving-Hockey saw last season in Chicago, where he faced top competition (90th percentile) with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

He's undrafted, a KHL graduate from Omsk, and still quick (73rd percentile in top speed). In Tampa he isn't asked to carry a line, and our projection of 13 to 23 goals reflects a useful middle-six winger, not more.
